task.name: A project cannot extend a sandbox capability preset, so a toolchain need the shipped presets do not anticipate has no configuration path
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A project whose gate requires the host Apple toolchain cannot build or test its
real app target under the sandbox, even with `sandbox.capability_profile: xcode`
selected and applied. The capability gap does not surface as a capability error —
it reaches the operator as a code-quality verdict.

In `hdp` run `70462a5b72a0`, story #248 ran three dev iterations, cost $10.03,
and ended `REQUEST_CHANGES`. Both blocking findings were the same objection
restated: the watch target was never built or exercised.

```
[P1] … A regression in the real watch alarm flow … would currently reach users
     without a failing test, because this change only exercised the pure
     scheduling helper …
[P1] … The watch alarm refactor still reached review without a successful
     app-scheme build, so the new watch-path source was only exercised through
     iOS unit tests and not through the real thebos target that embeds HDPWatch
```

The reviewer was correct on both counts. The dev agent could not comply, because
its own logs record three separate denials:

```
xcodebuild verification was blocked by sandbox constraints: CoreSimulator…
xcodebuild test` was blocked by a power-assertion denial
xcodebuild` cannot use CoreSimulator here, and package resolution cann[ot]…
```

The profile was in effect throughout — every dev invocation logs
`sandbox capability profile: xcode (6 extra write roots, 4 mach services)`.
The story was recorded as `review_rejected`, and the sprint's own NEXT advice was
to address the review findings and re-run, which would spend another cycle on a
finding no amount of dev work can resolve.

## Expected behavior

When a project declares that its gate depends on host toolchain capabilities, the
sandbox should either grant what that toolchain actually requires or fail the run
with an explicit capability error naming what was denied. A capability gap should
never reach the operator disguised as a code-quality verdict, because that routes
them toward more dev cycles against a condition no dev work can satisfy. A project
should also be able to express capability requirements that the shipped presets do
not anticipate, rather than being limited to selecting one whole preset or none;
the set of things a real toolchain needs is not knowable in advance from inside
this repository.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** with `capability_profile: xcode` applied, dev cannot run
  `xcodebuild` against a real app target; the resulting unverifiable code is
  rejected by review and the story is classified `review_rejected` rather than as
  an environment failure.

- **Evidence:** `hdp` run `70462a5b72a0` — profile application logged at
  `run-70462a5b72a0.log:165` (`sandbox capability profile: xcode (6 extra write
  roots, 4 mach services)`); the three denial messages above appear in
  `.forge/logs/issues-248,245,246,231/issue-248/*.log`; final verdict
  `REQUEST_CHANGES` with both P1s quoted above, $10.03 across three iterations.
  Inspecting the preset directly: `preset_names()` returns `('xcode',)`, and
  `get_preset('xcode').mach_services` is
  `com.apple.CoreSimulator.CoreSimulatorService`,
  `com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd`, `com.apple.lsd.mapdb`,
  `com.apple.system.notification_center`.


- **Correction (supersedes the original confirmed cause):** an earlier revision
  of this issue attributed the package-resolution failure to the absence of a
  network-egress concept in the preset model. That is wrong. The dev agent's own
  handoff in run `5096bd4a46e3` records the failure occurring against
  already-resolved derived data with all five package checkouts present, and
  persisting under `-disableAutomaticPackageResolution
  -onlyUsePackageVersionsFromResolvedFile -skipPackageUpdates`. Network was never
  reached. The failure is `sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`: SwiftPM
  compiles package manifests by invoking `sandbox-exec`, and macOS refuses to
  apply a sandbox inside the `sandbox-exec` confinement forge already established.
  Apple's documented workaround for that collision,
  `defaults write com.apple.dt.Xcode IDEPackageSupportDisableManifestSandbox`, is
  denied in turn because `~/Library/Preferences` is not a granted write root.

- **Confirmed cause:** two distinct defects were conflated here. The first is
  mechanical and not addressable by any grant: a toolchain that itself invokes
  `sandbox-exec` cannot run inside a `sandbox-exec` confinement, so no preset
  content and no extension to the preset model changes the outcome. That defect is
  tracked in #2050. What remains genuinely scoped to this issue is the capability
  model itself: `SandboxCapabilityPreset` carries only `name`, `description`,
  `supported_platforms`, `write_roots` and `mach_services`, and
  `config.types.SandboxConfig` exposes only `capability_profile: str | None`, so a
  project can select a whole preset but cannot add a write root, a mach service, or
  any other grant — and `xcode` remains the only preset. A project whose toolchain
  needs anything outside those grants has no configuration path, independently of
  the nesting collision.

- **Affected code path:** `config.sandbox_capabilities` —
  `SandboxCapabilityPreset`, `get_preset`, `preset_names`, `resolve_capabilities`;
  `config.types.SandboxConfig` (`config/types.py:614`) and
  `sandbox_capability_profile` (`config/types.py:258`).

- **Fix-success criterion:** a project can express a capability requirement the
  shipped presets do not anticipate — at minimum an additional write root and an
  additional mach service — without a code change in this repository, and a
  requirement that cannot be satisfied terminates the run with an explicit
  capability error naming what was denied.

## Notes

This issue has been narrowed. The two behaviors originally bundled here are now
tracked separately, because they have different causes and different fixes:

- #2050 — the dev agent cannot execute the project's declared toolchain. This is
  the nesting collision, and it is what actually blocks an Apple app-target build.
- #2051 — review blocks on agent-reported build evidence the run cannot produce
  while the coordinator holds its own gate result. This is the trust-ordering
  defect that turned the capability gap into a `review_rejected` verdict.
- #2029 — a capability gap is never surfaced as the actionable cause.

What remains here is the capability model: project-extensible grants. Whether the
model should also gain a network-egress concept is unresolved and, on the evidence
above, is not on the critical path for the observed failures — package resolution
failed with the cache fully populated and the network never reached.

[ADR-0007](docs/adr/0007-dev-phase-verification-capability.md) (Accepted 2026-07-29) owns the dev-phase
verification decision and records this issue as its **option C**: making the
capability model project-extensible is worth doing on its own merits but is
explicitly *not* the hdp unblock, because the nesting collision is not an
allowlist problem. No ADR owns the capability model itself.

`docs/adr/0004-execution-substrate.md` §9 records this ceiling as field evidence.
Its characterisation of the SwiftPM denial as a network-egress limitation carried
the same error corrected above and **has now been amended** (commit `c9ec55c`);
the §9 verdict is unaffected.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 3's runners/cli.py startup guard only addresses the initially selected transport. After a supported Claude or Gemini CLI starts, _maybe_run_api_fallback() directly invokes runner_api.run_api_agent() for both TransportFallbackConfig and fallback_models, bypassing run_agent's dispatch guard. A quota or model failure can therefore move a DEV profile carrying required grants onto an API transport that ignores them, violating the fail-closed acceptance criterion.
  Suggestion: Explicitly cover _maybe_run_api_fallback: refuse or suppress both legacy api_fallback and fallback_models whenever DEV capability grants are present and the fallback cannot express them, returning SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED with the denied roots/services. Add tests for this transition as well as direct API, Codex, and ghaw rejection.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 validates mach_services only as non-empty strings, but runners/sandbox.py interpolates each value directly into Seatbelt source in _macos_profile. A project value containing quotes/newlines can inject additional profile expressions, including broader grants, so the stated security mitigation is incomplete.
  Suggestion: Constrain mach-service entries to a safe service-name grammar or escape Seatbelt string literals, reject wildcard/control characters, and add a malicious-value regression test.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (transports that do not wrap through the host sandbox would silently ignore new grants) is retired at the design level by the Step 3 cli.py guard, but only partially at the test level: Step 4's runner assertions cover the existing runner_claude/runner_gemini SandboxCapabilityError -> SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED path (runner_claude.py:751-759, runner_gemini.py:196-204), not the new dispatcher guard for non-wrapping transports (runner_codex, runner_ghaw, api). Nothing would fail if the new guard were omitted.
  Suggestion: Add a runners/cli.py-level test that a DEV ModelProfile carrying project-declared write_roots/mach_services dispatched to a non-wrapping transport returns the SANDBOX_CAPABILITY_PROFILE_UNSUPPORTED startup failure rather than running unwrapped. Note the marker string currently lives only in runner_claude.py/runner_gemini.py; hoisting it to a shared constant avoids a third literal.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 changes ResolvedSandboxCapabilities.is_default to be false when custom grants exist. Verified: is_default has no production consumers today (only its definition at sandbox_capabilities.py:100 — the ForgeConfig *_is_default flags are unrelated), so this is safe, but the changed semantics ('default containment' vs 'no preset selected') should be reflected in the docstring since audit readers rely on it.
  Suggestion: Update the is_default docstring and the ResolvedSandboxCapabilities class docstring in the same step, and have audit_payload emit the project-declared additions distinguishably from preset grants so a reviewer can tell which grant came from where.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 keeps _REJECTED_INLINE_SANDBOX_KEYS rejecting exactly the keys it now needs to accept — write_roots/mach_services are currently in that frozenset (config/load.py:102), with an error message stating forge.yaml 'supports only forge-owned named presets'. Also the module docstring of config/sandbox_capabilities.py states a project 'cannot author, extend, or override' a preset, which this story deliberately reverses.
  Suggestion: Explicitly remove write_roots/mach_services from _REJECTED_INLINE_SANDBOX_KEYS (leaving allow_default/disabled/mode rejected), reword the remaining rejection message, and amend the sandbox_capabilities module docstring so the stated invariant matches the shipped behaviour.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
